extracted.intended_audience: Commissioner of Indian Affairs, Office of Indian Affairs, agency superintendents, policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: An annual United States Indian Agency administrative report (Standing Rock, 1880) describing management and condition of the reservation across domains such as education, agriculture, police, transportation, health, religion, housing, and allotments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote self-sustaining labor and husbandry
rubrics_metrics.description: The government should afford Indians facilities for gratifying their taste for husbandry, encouraging them to labor and become self-sustaining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although attending with expense, such outlay is 'well spent' and 'eventually be regarded as legitimate economy.' When Indians perceive compensation for labor they will apply themselves to accumulation of wealth and property, which leads to influence and gradual civilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop latent ingenuity and mechanical skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide shops and suitable tools so Indians may make their own repairs and develop latent ingenuity and mechanical skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent encourages Indians bringing wood-work for repairs; the government has power to develop mechanical skill by erecting shops and furnishing tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education — boarding school effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Boarding schools (e.g., Carlisle) have a salutary effect; a boarding-school located reasonably remote from the agency would accomplish more than day-schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Day-school at the agency was unsuccessful due to lack of application and demoralizing surroundings. The agent is estimating cost, plans, and specifications for a boarding-school for 50 scholars and recommends remote location to improve educational and civilizing outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education — attendance and literacy metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Track average monthly attendance, numbers able to read English and Dakota, and numbers who learned to read during the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example statistics: average attendance 81, largest average 100; numbers able to read both English and Dakota 60, Dakota only 65, English only 123; number learned during year 19. Use these measures to assess school impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher performance and context sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess teachers by zeal and industry but recognize pupil inclination and local circumstances may limit observable success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Female teachers received 'highest praise' though labors were not crowned with complete success attributable to causes other than their perseverance; day-school failures tied to surroundings and pupil inclination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religion — missionary oversight and conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Religious interests are assessed by missionary supervision and the number brought to 'the knowledge of the truth.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resident missionary's godly life and Christian influence cited as measure of success; religious interests 'could not be placed in better hands.' Track church membership and mission activity (church buildings under construction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicine — physician effectiveness and transition from traditional healers
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure medical success by the agency physician's treatment and cure of climate-incident and hereditary maladies and reduction in reliance on 'quack' Indian doctors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dr. Faulkner's medical skill and perseverance credited with bringing about abandonment of superstitious treatments; medical outcomes should be recorded as indicator of public health progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation — Indian freighting capacity and trustworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate transportation by Indians via measures: distances (e.g., 92 miles), pounds of freight carried, timeliness of round trips, care of wagons/animals, and economic terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: one Indian returned in <5 days with 3,600 pounds; Indians transported all freight since establishment except one season; number engaged (230), teams (230), pounds (87,183), amount paid ($348.73). Use these data to justify contracting freight to Indians instead of white freighters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Police — selection, discipline, and loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Police should be selected per Office of Indian Affairs instructions from best and truest Indians, pro rata from each band; duties and obligations must be made known and disinclined allowed to withdraw.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure police by intelligence, obedience, training (army experience considered), number of complaints, and pride in execution of orders. Address selection abuses (e.g., chiefs appointing forces) and ensure force allegiance to federal authority rather than individual chiefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Police — uniform, pay, and equal treatment complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Police expressed grievances when treated differently than white soldiers (uniform color, pay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and consider complaints such as why Indian police wear gray while other soldiers wear blue and why pay differs; these affect morale and perceived fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law enforcement event response and detention procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle disturbances and criminal acts with a mix of firmness and kindness, securing arrests, holding prisoners under guard, and delivering them to civil authorities for trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples: dispersing unlawful postings by police, arrest of horse-stealing raiders, transporting prisoners safely to Fort Randall, and cooperating with chiefs like Spotted Tail and Crow Dog. Use patience and decisive action to avert disaster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agriculture — production, acreage, and mechanization
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure agricultural progress by bushels produced (wheat, oats, corn, potatoes), acres cultivated/broken, number of farmers and sizes of fields, and adoption of machinery (reapers, fanning mills, self-binder).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: estimated 1880 wheat 24,000 bu., oats 5,600 bu., corn 6,500 bu., potatoes 15,000 bu.; acres cultivated 4,025; track purchases of reapers, mills, rakes and local purchase of seed-wheat as indicators of improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annuities distribution — tools vs subsistence
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference to distribute tools, wagons, working cattle, and housebuilding materials over sustained supplies of food to promote independence as annuities approach cessation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record numbers of tools distributed (e.g., 95 yokes, 115 wagons, 270 plows, 180 harrows) and note community desire for tools/materials rather than ongoing food/clothing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing — construction, crowding, and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Track houses built for Indians and employees, types (frame, log), materials purchase (pine lumber, shingles), and occupancy (e.g., 35 houses with ~6 persons each indicating crowding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use annuity appropriations to buy lumber; encourage Indians to furnish logs and do construction. Recommend building more frame houses as a 'civilizing influence' and for health improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary conditions and health infrastructure need
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess sanitary state by birth/death statistics and observe need for small hospital to reduce death rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example figures: births 42, deaths 36. Note difficulties with food preparation, regular meals, and compliance with physician's directives as contributory factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schools — sustainment and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustain all schools and record funding sources and amounts (government vs other sources) as indicators of educational support and success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: funds expended for educational purposes — from government $1,950; from other sources $1,250. Agent stresses necessity of sustaining schools despite slow progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious institutions — membership and building activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure religious activity by number of churches, membership totals, and construction of church buildings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: five Presbyterian churches with total membership 426 (Indians 416, whites 10); missions constructing new frame church buildings of specified dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allotments and land patents — administrative completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Allotments/patents to Indians require completion of township plats to show fractional sections; lack of plats delays issuance of patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record progress on papers and note impediments (e.g., need for township plats) to finishing allotment business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infrastructure improvements to reduce external contracting
rubrics_metrics.description: Invest in local mills and sawmills (engine, burrs, gearing) to increase on-site production (flour) and reduce contracted deliveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department furnished new engine and saw-mill gearing; repair of mill building and machinery expected to reduce milling contract quantity and cost over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land claims activity — recording claims opened and farm inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: Record claims taken/opened by Indians and maintain detailed inspections of Indian-managed farms (what planted, fenced status, hay, acreage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive schedules of individual farms, crops planted, fenced status, and claims taken/opened provide granular measures of settlement, cultivation, and land tenure activity.
